spec: Validate a Base64-encoded string format: the length must be a positive multiple of 4, at most the last 2 characters may be '=' padding characters (occurring only at the very end), and every non-padding character must be a letter (upper or lower case), digit, '+', or '/'. Return False otherwise.
Compute the sum of all positive divisors of a positive integer n that are themselves even numbers.

Given a list of item names and a dict mapping some item names to a category string, count how many items fall into each category. Items not present in the categories dict are counted under 'other'. Return a dict mapping category to count. An empty items list returns an empty dict.
Find the smallest prime number that is strictly greater than the integer n.
Given a year and a non-negative integer n, return the (month, day) tuple of the date that is n days before December 31st of that year (n=0 means December 31st itself), accounting for leap years.
Compute the sum of all prime numbers strictly less than n that belong to a twin prime pair (a prime p qualifies if p-2 or p+2 is also prime).

For each position in the list items, compute how many times that element has occurred so far, counting the current occurrence (i.e. a running per-value tally). Return a list of these running counts, one per input element, in order. An empty list returns an empty list.

Given a full name of one or more whitespace-separated words, keep only the first and last words (dropping any middle names), joined by a single space. If the name has one or two words, return it unchanged (words joined by a single space).
Lowercase the filename and replace every space with a hyphen, then remove any character that is not a lowercase letter, digit, hyphen, or period.

Given a list of strings, return them sorted by the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) they contain, ascending. If two strings have the same vowel count, order them alphabetically. The input list may be empty.
Compute the sum of the squares of all positive divisors of a positive integer n.

Given a string s, count how often each pair of adjacent characters occurs, using the two-character substring as the key. Return a dict mapping each bigram string to its count. A string with fewer than two characters returns an empty dict.
Compute the number of trailing zeros in the decimal representation of n! (n factorial) for a non-negative integer n, without necessarily computing n! itself.
submission:
def trailing_zeros_factorial(n):
    count = 0
    power = 5
    while power <= n:
        count += n // power
        power *= 5
    return count

spec: Given two equal-length lists keys and values, build a dict by pairing them positionally. If a key appears more than once, keep the value from its last occurrence, overwriting earlier ones. Empty lists return an empty dict.

Write a function that finds the indices of interior 'peaks' in a list of numbers, where a peak is an element strictly greater than both of its immediate neighbors. The first and last elements can never be peaks. Return the 0-indexed positions of all peaks, in increasing order, as a list. Return an empty list if the list has fewer than 3 elements or has no peaks.

Write a function that takes a list of strings and a minimum length, and returns a new list containing only the strings whose length is greater than or equal to that minimum, preserving order. The input list may be empty and the minimum length may be zero.

Given a list of (name, score) tuples and an integer k, return the names of the k lowest-scoring entries as a list, lowest score first. When two entries have the same score, the one with the alphabetically earlier name comes first. If k exceeds the number of entries, return all names in this order.
Given a year, a month (1-12) and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), return how many times that weekday occurs in that month (either 4 or 5).

Return a new list of the same length as the input, where the element at each index is the maximum value seen among the input elements from the start up to and including that index. An empty list returns an empty list.

Convert a string into a slug the same way as ordinary slugification but using underscores instead of hyphens as the separator: lowercase the text, replace every run of characters that are not lowercase letters or digits with a single underscore, and strip leading/trailing underscores.
Split a list of integers into two lists, preserving relative order: one containing the even numbers and one containing the odd numbers. Return them together as a tuple (evens, odds).
Determine whether a positive integer n is a (generalized, only-positive-index) pentagonal number, i.e. n = k*(3*k-1)/2 for some positive integer k.

Write a function that returns the values located at interior 'peaks' of a list of numbers, where a peak is an element strictly greater than both of its immediate neighbors. The first and last elements can never be peaks. Return the peak values, in the order their positions occur in the list. Return an empty list if there are no peaks.

Count the number of positions in a string where two consecutive alphabetic characters differ in case (one uppercase and the other lowercase), scanning through the whole string. Pairs where either character is not alphabetic are not counted.

Given a list of item names, a dictionary mapping each name to a category, and a priority list of categories, reorder the items so that all items whose category is the first priority category come first (in their original relative order), then all items of the second priority category, and so on. Items whose category is not in the priority list come last, keeping their original relative order.

Given a string s, return a copy with characters swapped in adjacent pairs: the character at index 0 swaps with the character at index 1, index 2 swaps with index 3, and so on. If s has odd length, the final unpaired character stays in its original place.

Given a digit string and a count keep, mask every character except the last keep characters, replacing masked characters with '*' and keeping the total length unchanged. If keep is zero or negative, mask the whole string; if keep is greater than or equal to the string's length, return the string unchanged.

Given a year, a month (1-12), a starting day-of-month, and a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday), return the day-of-month (an integer) of the last occurrence of that weekday on or before the given day, guaranteed to still fall in the same month.

Write a function that takes a list and a positive integer k, and returns a new list with every element removed whose 0-indexed position (first element is position 0) is a multiple of k, preserving the order of the remaining elements. If k is less than or equal to 0, return a copy of the list unchanged.

Given a list of lowercase words, group the words that are anagrams of each other (contain the same letters with the same frequency). Return a list of groups, where each group is a list of the original words in their original relative order, and the groups themselves are ordered by the first appearance of any word belonging to that group.
Given a date string in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format, parse it and return the corresponding (year, month, day) tuple of integers (with no leading zeros in the integers).

Validate a plain integer string: an optional leading '+' or '-' sign, followed by digits with no leading zero unless the value is exactly '0' (a sign followed directly by '0' with more digits after is invalid). Return False otherwise.

Given a string s and a positive integer min_run, compress s by replacing every maximal run of identical consecutive characters whose length is at least min_run with that character followed by its run length as digits; runs shorter than min_run are left as their original, uncompressed characters. An empty string returns an empty string.
Given an email address whose local part (before the '@') consists of dot-separated name components, return the uppercase initials formed from the first letter of each component, in order.

Validate a scientific notation number string of the form 'digits(.digits)?e digits' where an optional sign may precede the mantissa digits and an optional sign may precede the exponent digits, and the exponent marker may be lowercase 'e' or uppercase 'E' (e.g. '6.022e23', '-1.5E-10', '2e5'). Return False otherwise.

Write a function that finds the second smallest distinct value in a list of numbers (duplicates of the smallest value do not count as separate values). Return None if the list has fewer than two distinct values.

Given the current time and a target time, both expressed as an integer number of seconds since midnight (0 to 86399), return the number of seconds remaining until the target. If the target has already passed today (its value is less than or equal to current, but not exactly equal), assume it occurs at that time tomorrow instead. If they are exactly equal, return 0.
Return the number of days in a given month of a given year, where month is an integer from 1 (January) to 12 (December). Account for leap years when computing the length of February.

Given a string s, consider only its digit characters in order (ignoring all non-digit characters, which do not break adjacency between digits) and count the number of adjacent digit pairs where the second digit is strictly greater than the first. A string with fewer than two digits returns 0.

Given a non-empty list of integers, for each element compute the percentage of elements in the list that are strictly smaller than it (count of smaller elements divided by the list length, times 100), rounded to 2 decimal places. Return the list of these percentages in the same order as the input.
